ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory automated and manual screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against (i) EU consolidated financial sanctions list (incl. Russia/Belarus and human-rights sanctions per Reg. (EU) 269/2014), (ii) French Ministère de l'Économie sanctions/asset-freeze database (Gels avoirs – Direction Générale du Trésor), (iii) UN Security Council consolidated list, (iv) OFAC/SDN list, (v) FATF public statements, and (vi) TRACFIN reporting thresholds; PEP status assessed per Article L.561-10 CMF with enhanced due diligence (EDD) mandatory when a PEP is a UBO, legal representative, or beneficial intermediary; ongoing transaction monitoring and suspicious-transaction reporting under Articles L.561-15 and L.561-25 CMF.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.aml_risk_tier_assessment: Low_Risk_Standard for packaged food manufacturing with SWIFT LC/TT payment rails, subject to CDD verification of all UBOs and licensing authorities.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: INPI / Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); name availability verified via the RCS national database and Infogreffe (data.inpi.fr, ARIANE search)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company name may be foreign-language but must use Latin script for RCS registration; a French or pinyin-based Latin transliteration is recommended for any Chinese brand; all statutory documents, annexes, food labels, and consumer-facing materials must be in French per Law No. 94-665 of 4 Aug 1994 (Toubon Law); statute drafting is required to be in French (Article L.224-2 Code de commerce); food-product labelling in French is mandatory under Article R.112-10 Code de la consommation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: National / République / État (when implying state affiliation)
SA / SAS / EURL / SARL (when used incorrectly as pure brand tokens)
Champagne, Roquefort, Gruyère, and all protected designations of origin (AOC/AOP/IGP) without authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: 1) If the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (via the Guichet unique) issues a formal rejection, counsel may re-submit an amended filing with a disambiguated name within the RCS 30-day reservation window; 2) Where refusal is grounded on distinctiveness or prior rights, the applicant may apply ex parte to the President of the Tribunal de Commerce (référé, Article L.123-35 C. com.) for an order compelling registration; 3) Trademark-related refusals by INPI may be appealed through a formal opposition within two months of BOPI publication; 4) Secondary recourse lies to the Cour d'appel and, on questions of law, to the Cour de Cassation; 5) Where name conflict arises from third-party rights, the applicant may alternatively initiate a settlement / coexistence agreement or modify the corporate name post-incorporation (with shareholders' resolution and RCS amendment) to avoid litigation costs.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.bullseye_name_selection_guidance: For an SAS manufacturing Luosifen-style instant rice noodles, a distinctive Latin-script brand such as 'LUO RIVER FOOD SAS' or 'SNAIL NOODLE FRANCE SAS' with French co-title is recommended; prior INPI trademark availability and RCS similarity searches must be performed and documented.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for the SAS administrative registered office only via a certified société de domiciliation (NF 345-1 standard) per Articles L.123-37 and L.123-38 C. com. (max. 5 years for domiciliation contracts); the food-manufacturing production facility must be a separate, physically staffed establishment registered with the DDPP/DGCCRF, holding all sanitary approvals and subject to EU Regulation 178/2002 traceability requirements; hybrid model is common and compliant continental practice.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Registered office: 20% likelihood of a routine inspection in the first operational year (registry and tax control). Production facility: 90% likelihood of an unannounced DGCCRF/DDPP inspection within 12 months of first production run, per Title V of EU Regulation 2017/625 (Official Controls Regulation); food-composition and hygiene audits are standard for retort/instant noodle manufacturing.

stage_1.compliance_opinion: Stage-1 pre-incorporation due diligence confirms that a French SAS is a lawful and low-risk vehicle for the manufacture and canning of retort river snail noodles (Luosifen), provided that (i) all UBO documents are apostilled and sworn-translated before filing; (ii) mandatory RBE declaration accompanies the RCS application; (iii) the food production establishment obtains sanitary approval and complies with EU Regulation 178/2002 and 2017/625; and (iv) the company name avoids protected tokens. Estimated total stage-1 budget: USD 7,915.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L. 227-1 to L. 227-20 (SAS), and Articles R. 123-1 et seq. (RCS registration)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), administered by INPI via the Guichet Unique (https://procedures.inpi.fr)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts constitutifs (Articles of Association) and Déclaration de création d'entreprise (incorporation filing)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for SAS; capital may be freely set in statuts. Funds must be deposited in a blocked corporate bank account until RCS registration, then released to the company.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The undersigned, acting as sole director (Président) of [Company Name] SAS, hereby resolves: (1) to approve the subscription of [number] shares at [amount] euros per share, fully paid in cash; (2) to adopt the registered office at [address]; (3) to appoint [Name] as Président and [Name] as Directeur Général for an unlimited term; and (4) to authorise the Président to file all necessary documents with the RCS. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and notarise Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaire (French notary) or private deed under Article L. 227-1
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a French notary to draft the statuts, specifying corporate purpose (manufacture and canning of retort river snail noodles), share capital, governance, and registered office. All founding shareholders must sign. For a SAS with non-resident shareholders, a notarised power of attorney is recommended.
required_dossiers: Proof of registered office (lease or domiciliation contract)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary rejects the statuts due to non-compliant clauses, revise the corporate purpose, capital, or governance provisions and re-submit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit share capital in a blocked bank account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French bank or notary escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate bank account. Deposit the full subscribed capital in cash. Obtain a certificate de dépôt de fonds from the bank or notary. Funds remain blocked until RCS registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to open an account due to non-resident status, use a notary escrow account or a digital bank specialising in non-resident company formation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish legal notice in a journal of legal announcements
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish a notice containing company name, legal form, capital, registered office, and director information. Obtain an attestation de parution from the JAL.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL rejects the notice, correct the mandatory information and republish within the same department.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File incorporation dossier with the Guichet Unique (INPI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique (online portal) for RCS and tax registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the full dossier electronically: statuts, certificate de dépôt de fonds, attestation de parution, proof of office, director declarations, and beneficial owner declaration. Pay the RCS filing fee. The dossier is forwarded to the greffe and tax authorities.
required_dossiers: Director ID and declaration of non-conviction
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the dossier is queried (rejet), correct the identified defect within 15 days and re-submit via the Guichet Unique without additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Kbis extract and register for taxes
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de commerce (Kbis) and Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, download the Kbis extract from the INPI portal. The DGFiP automatically assigns a SIRET and VAT number. If not, file a separate tax registration (Formulaire M0).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SIRET is not issued, contact the SIE (Service des Impôts des Entreprises) with the Kbis and statuts to manually register.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Départementale de la Protection des Populations (DDPP) and Direction Régionale de l'Alimentation, de l'Agriculture et de la Forêt (DRAAF)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Déclaration d'activité de fabrication de denrées animales ou d'origine animale (Article 6 of Regulation (EC) No 852/2004) and agrément sanitaire if using animal by-products

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Déclaration avec contrôle périodique (DC) under ICPE rubric 2220 (food processing) if daily production capacity exceeds 500 kg but below thresholds for Enregistrement; otherwise Enregistrement (E) if capacity exceeds 2 tonnes/day
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Arrêté Ministériel du 02/02/1998 for food processing: wastewater COD ≤ 300 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 100 mg/L, TSS ≤ 100 mg/L; VOC emissions from cooking and packaging must not exceed 110 mg/m³; solid waste must be sorted and sent to approved facilities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification by the SDIS (Service Départemental d'Incendie et de Secours) under the Code de la construction et de l'habitation; structural load inspection by a bureau de contrôle (e.g., Bureau Veritas); workplace clearance from the Inspection du Travail for ventilation, noise, and ergonomic standards.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: The competent authority is the Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), under the Ministry of the Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty. A French SAS is generally registered through the business-formalities single window (Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises), which transmits formation information to the relevant authorities. Corporate tax and VAT filings and payments are handled through the DGFiP professional online account (Espace professionnel) on impots.gouv.fr. A non-established foreign taxable person is generally handled by the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères (SIEE).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: On incorporation, file the SAS formation formalities through the Guichet unique. Following registration in the Registre national des entreprises and, where applicable, the commercial and companies register, the company receives a SIREN identifier and establishment-specific SIRET identifier; these are not, by themselves, a VAT number. For VAT-taxable activity, request VAT identification from the competent business tax office, providing corporate registration documents, a description of activity, expected transactions, establishment and representative details, and evidence supporting the need for registration. A French VAT number generally takes the form FR followed by a two-digit key and the SIREN. Non-EU businesses without a French establishment generally apply through the SIEE and may be required to appoint a French fiscal representative; qualifying businesses established in the EU are generally not required to appoint one. Register for the DGFiP professional online account to file and pay applicable taxes. Obtain an EORI number separately through French customs when required for customs operations. Confirm the applicable registration route and document list with the DGFiP or customs authority before commencing transactions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A French SAS is ordinarily subject to French corporation tax (impôt sur les sociétés, or IS) on its taxable profits; the standard rate is generally 25%, subject to applicable reduced-rate conditions and other statutory provisions. An eligible newly formed SAS may elect temporary taxation under the income-tax regime for a limited period, generally up to five financial years, only if statutory ownership, activity, size, age, and other conditions are satisfied and the required shareholder consent and filing formalities are met. Certain qualifying family-owned companies may have a separate election route, subject to statutory conditions. France does not provide a general US-style check-the-box election for an SAS. Classification and elections should be assessed against current French law and the company’s facts.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT; taxe sur la valeur ajoutée or TVA), operating under the harmonized European Union VAT system.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a French-established SAS, the domestic small-business VAT exemption (franchise en base) may apply only if the applicable statutory turnover conditions are met and no disqualifying circumstances or voluntary election apply. The commonly applicable thresholds for domestic supplies are EUR 85,000 for supplies of goods and EUR 37,500 for services, subject to statutory reference-period rules, transitional provisions, and legislative changes. A manufacturer making taxable supplies should verify the applicable thresholds and eligibility for the relevant tax year. A business that is liable to VAT or opts to charge VAT must register as required. A non-established taxable person generally cannot assume that the domestic small-business exemption is available; registration may be required from the first taxable transaction, subject to applicable EU schemes and rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing domestic B2B electronic invoicing and transaction/payment data reporting in phases. From 1 September 2026, all businesses in scope must be able to receive electronic invoices; issuance obligations are scheduled to apply from that date to large and intermediate-sized businesses and from 1 September 2027 to small and medium-sized businesses, subject to current implementation rules. In-scope invoices must be transmitted through an approved platform (plateforme agréée) and conform to prescribed formats and data requirements. Relevant cross-border and business-to-consumer transactions, and certain payment data, are subject to electronic reporting rather than domestic B2B invoice transmission. France does not generally require real-time tax-authority clearance or digital stamping of each invoice. Confirm scope, platform requirements, exemptions, and effective dates against current DGFiP guidance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods dispatched or transported from France to a destination outside the European Union, the supply may be exempt from French VAT with the right to deduct input VAT when statutory export conditions are met and the supplier can substantiate that the goods left the EU customs territory. The supplier should retain consistent commercial, transport, accounting, and customs evidence and report the transaction correctly. A sale to an EU customer is generally treated under intra-Community supply rules, not export rules; exemption depends on the applicable conditions, including the customer’s valid VAT identification and evidence of transport to another Member State. Services are not automatically zero-rated because the customer is offshore: place-of-supply rules determine whether French VAT applies, and any exemption or outside-scope treatment must be supported by the service type, customer status, and evidence. Input VAT recovery remains subject to ordinary deduction restrictions and documentation requirements.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export customs declaration and evidence of exit from the EU customs territory, including the customs export result or equivalent exit confirmation
Commercial invoice, sales contract or purchase order, and accounting records identifying the goods and the foreign customer
Bill of lading, air waybill, CMR consignment note, or other transport document, as applicable
Carrier, freight-forwarder, delivery, or other corroborating evidence linking the goods to the export declaration and destination
Customer payment and bank records where relevant to substantiate the transaction; an inward remittance certificate is not a general French statutory prerequisite for export VAT exemption
For intra-Community supplies rather than exports, the customer’s VAT identification evidence and proof of dispatch or transport to another EU Member State
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: There is no general French statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline of 180 days applicable to export VAT zero-rating. The supplier bears the burden of substantiating the export exemption and should retain records for the applicable statutory retention and audit periods. If export or exemption conditions are not established, the DGFiP may assess output VAT, late-payment interest, and applicable penalties. French tax penalties can include a 40% surcharge for deliberate failure and an 80% surcharge in specified cases of fraudulent activity or abuse, in addition to interest; the applicable sanction depends on the facts and legal characterization. Incorrect input VAT deductions or VAT refunds may also be reassessed, recovered, and penalized. A fraudulent declaration may entail additional civil or criminal consequences.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France is France’s central bank and participates in the Eurosystem. The European Central Bank sets euro-area monetary policy. The French Treasury (Direction générale du Trésor) administers applicable financial sanctions and certain capital-control measures.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France has no general exchange controls restricting conversion or cross-border transfer of euros or other currencies. Current-account payments, including trade payments, are generally freely transferable, subject to sanctions, anti-money-laundering, counter-terrorist-financing, tax, and documentary requirements. Capital movements are also generally free under EU law, subject to narrowly applicable statutory restrictions, sanctions, and reporting obligations. Dividends, interest, and other profits may generally be remitted without exchange-control approval after applicable French corporate approvals, withholding-tax analysis, treaty or EU-relief documentation, and tax filings. Banks may require evidence of the underlying transaction, source of funds, beneficial ownership, and tax status. French-resident companies must assess any applicable Banque de France balance-of-payments statistical reporting and declare foreign accounts where required; these are reporting obligations, not general remittance permissions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. Export proceeds may generally be retained in euros or foreign currency and held domestically or abroad, subject to bank terms, sanctions screening, accounting and tax rules, and applicable statistical reporting. There is no general statutory deadline requiring conversion of export receipts. Cash or monetary instruments physically transported across the EU external border with an aggregate value of EUR 10,000 or more are subject to EU cash-control declaration requirements; separate French and EU reporting rules may apply to particular transactions or financial intermediaries.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for routine payments, subject to the provider’s country, customer, currency, and transaction coverage. An EU-authorised electronic money institution may provide payment and e-money services under its authorisation and passporting rights, but e-money is not a bank deposit and generally is not covered by the deposit-guarantee scheme. An EMI account is not automatically suitable for statutory share-capital deposits, escrow, credit, documentary trade finance, or all SWIFT/LC needs. Verify the provider’s authorisation in the relevant regulator register, safeguarding arrangements, transfer limits, sanctions controls, and ability to receive the intended capital or trade payments. Use an authorised credit institution for capital-deposit certification or escrow where legally or contractually required.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal requirement that directors attend a bank branch in person to open a corporate account. Remote onboarding may be available, but each bank determines its risk-based procedures and may require an in-person or video interview, wet signatures, certified or apostilled documents, or an appearance by an authorised representative. Non-resident shareholders or directors, complex ownership, higher-risk geographies, or unusual funding flows can trigger enhanced due diligence and delay or refusal. Confirm onboarding requirements before incorporation funding or transaction deadlines.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear ultimate beneficial ownership, layered foreign holding companies, nominee arrangements, or inability to identify natural-person beneficial owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide current corporate registry extracts and constitutional documents for each ownership layer; a dated ownership chart through to natural-person beneficial owners; identity and address evidence; beneficial-owner register filing evidence where applicable; board resolutions; and a clear explanation of control, economic rights, and any nominee or trust arrangement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital contribution or operating funds originating from an unrelated third party, high-risk jurisdiction, opaque intermediary, or source inconsistent with the company’s profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide subscription or shareholder-loan agreements, shareholder and board approvals, originating-bank statements, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence, audited accounts or tax records where relevant, and a transaction-by-transaction explanation linking the remitter, beneficial owner, and French SAS.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained high-volume international receipts or payments, circular flows, payments to unrelated parties, or material divergence between account activity and the packaged-food manufacturing business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a 12-month cash-flow forecast, customer and supplier lists, signed contracts or purchase orders, invoices, shipping and customs records, Incoterms, expected countries and currencies, payment-flow diagrams, and documented approval controls for new counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Food manufacturing, import, or export activity lacking evidence of applicable food-business registration, establishment compliance, or product-safety controls.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the company’s relevant food-business registration or establishment documentation, facility and production details, food-safety and traceability procedures, product specifications and labels, supplier and ingredient records, and import/export documentation. Confirm the exact requirements with the competent French authorities for the products and activities involved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions exposure, restricted-party matches, transactions involving sanctioned destinations or counterparties, or trade in goods subject to restrictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide documented screening results for the company, beneficial owners, counterparties, banks, vessels, and relevant goods; applicable licences or authorisations where required; contract and shipping documentation; and a written escalation and transaction-blocking procedure. Do not process a transaction until a potential match is resolved.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Fund the SAS through a documented equity subscription or shareholder loan from the identified investor’s account, using an EU/SEPA credit transfer for euros or a bank-to-bank SWIFT transfer for non-euro funds. Use the correct beneficiary name and IBAN/BIC, state the true payment purpose, and retain the subscription or loan agreement, corporate approvals, remitter statements, source-of-funds evidence, and bank confirmations. There is no universal French FX purpose-code regime requiring a specific code for ordinary corporate capital transfers; supply accurate payment details and any bank-requested statistical or compliance classification. For incorporation, deposit share capital with an eligible depositary and obtain the required deposit certificate before release in accordance with the formation process. Reconcile incoming funds to the shareholder register and accounting records, and assess applicable Banque de France, tax, and foreign-account reporting obligations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within SEPA and SWIFT customer credit transfers, commonly MT103 or its ISO 20022 equivalent, for cross-border payments outside SEPA or in other currencies. For imports or larger documented trade obligations, an issuing bank may arrange a documentary commercial letter of credit, subject to credit approval, facility terms, and applicable documentary-credit rules; documentary collection may be an alternative. Match each payment to the contract, invoice, purchase order, transport and customs records, and counterparty screening. Agree currency, Incoterms, bank charges, payment milestones, and required documents contractually. Retain payment confirmations and reconcile FX conversions, fees, VAT/customs records, and accounting entries.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward contracts for documented foreign-currency exposures, subject to the bank’s suitability, credit, collateral, and documentation requirements.

Non-deliverable forwards where commercially available and appropriate for a restricted or non-deliverable currency; settlement terms and regulatory treatment depend on the currency, counterparty, and contract.

Currency swaps or cross-currency swaps for documented liquidity or funding needs, subject to counterparty credit approval, collateral terms, and applicable derivatives reporting and risk-management requirements.
Vanilla FX options may be available for documented exposures, subject to product governance, suitability or appropriateness requirements, pricing, and credit terms.

Assess whether MiFID II, EMIR, and related EU rules apply, including classification, reporting, risk-mitigation, clearing, and margin obligations where relevant. Non-financial counterparties should document their classification and monitor applicable clearing thresholds; do not hedge beyond a supportable commercial exposure without appropriate legal and treasury controls.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts by the shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders of the SAS; the company must retain the approval decision in its corporate records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end, unless a court grants an extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A court may order the president to convene the shareholders and impose a daily penalty. Failure to approve alone does not trigger automatic strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of approved annual accounts and related required documents
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial and Companies Registry (Registre du commerce et des sociétés) through the competent commercial court registry (greffe)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval, or within two months if filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The registry or an interested party may seek a court order to file, potentially with a daily penalty; a fifth-class contravention may attract a fine of up to EUR 1,500. Late filing does not by itself cause automatic strike-off; any ex officio removal requires a separate statutory process and notice.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) is generally required when the SAS exceeds at least two of these thresholds at year-end: EUR 5 million total assets, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 average employees. Special rules apply to groups and certain regulated entities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French generally accepted accounting principles under the Plan comptable général (PCG). IFRS applies to consolidated accounts where required, including for listed groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no general annual UBO confirmation filing. The SAS must file updated beneficial-ownership information with the registry within 30 days after a reportable change. Share transfers and corporate decisions must be recorded in the relevant share and decision records.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of shareholders and share movements
Register of share accounts, where applicable
Minutes and written decisions of shareholders and corporate bodies

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 220–1,100 per year for commercial domiciliation; location and services affect pricing
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 2,200–6,600 per year for a small SAS subject to statutory audit; complexity and group scope may increase fees

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés). A 3.3% social contribution may apply to companies meeting the applicable turnover and tax thresholds, producing an effective rate of approximately 25.83%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Eligible small and medium-sized companies may apply a 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to the statutory conditions, including turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million, paid-up capital, and qualifying ownership. Certain newly established businesses, innovation activities, and investment projects may qualify for separate statutory regimes or tax credits. The research tax credit is generally 30% of qualifying research expenditure up to EUR 100 million and 5% above that threshold. Tax credits are subject to specific eligibility, documentation, and anti-abuse rules.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited. The annual utilization of carried-forward tax losses is generally capped at EUR 1 million plus 50% of the portion of current-year taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. The unused balance remains available indefinitely. Loss carryback is generally limited to the immediately preceding accounting period and is subject to a EUR 1 million cap.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD, Déclaration de résultats soumise à l'impôt sur les sociétés, together with the applicable 2058-A-SD through 2059-G-SD tax tables, filed electronically through the French tax administration's EDI-TDFC channel or an approved filing intermediary. Form 2572-SD is used for the corporate income tax balance payment. Form 2069-RCI-SD is used for centralized reporting of eligible tax credits.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; corporate income tax instalments are generally paid quarterly, with an annual balance payment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return is generally due within three months after the end of the accounting period. For a financial year ending on 31 December, the return is generally due by the second business day following 1 May of the following year. The final corporate income tax balance is generally payable by the 15th day of the fourth month following the accounting period-end, subject to the statutory calendar and electronic payment rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, French SIREN number, registered office, tax office, accounting period, legal form, and date of year-end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder or parent does not replace the French SAS as the taxpayer. Report the French SAS's registered office, SIREN, French tax office, and French accounting period. Report foreign parent details only where a schedule specifically requests group, ownership, or related-party information.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit or tax loss after reconciliation of statutory accounts with French tax rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only income and deductible expenditure attributable to the French SAS. Do not include the foreign shareholder's worldwide income or the foreign parent's profit unless a French permanent establishment or another specific allocation rule applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation from accounting result to taxable result, including non-deductible expenses, tax-exempt income, provisions, capital gains, depreciation adjustments, and other permanent or temporary differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify expenses paid to non-residents, intra-group charges, royalties, interest, management fees, and other cross-border items separately in the accounting records and supporting schedules. Apply French deductibility, withholding tax, interest limitation, and anti-hybrid rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses available from prior years, losses utilized in the current year, and remaining losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the French SAS's own losses only. A foreign parent's losses cannot be imported into France absent a specific statutory regime. Apply the EUR 1 million plus 50% annual utilization limitation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, foreign tax credits where available, tax credit carryforwards, and other tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim treaty or domestic foreign tax relief only where the French SAS is legally entitled to it and retains evidence of foreign tax paid, income source, beneficial ownership, and treaty entitlement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Short-term and long-term capital gains, losses, and applicable exemptions or special rates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident seller's share disposal is not automatically reported as ordinary French SAS income. Report transactions of the French SAS and separately assess French-source taxation, withholding, and real-estate-rich entity rules for non-resident shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Value added and production-related information used for tax computation or statistical purposes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the French entity's French accounting and operational data. Do not consolidate foreign group turnover unless the form or relevant tax rule expressly requires group information.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Summary declaration of eligible tax credits, including research, apprenticeship, and other qualifying credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign parent cannot claim a French SAS tax credit merely because it funds the activity. The French SAS must satisfy the substantive French eligibility conditions and retain contemporaneous technical and expenditure documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Summary of the group's transfer-pricing policy, controlled transactions, methods, and financial information where the statutory filing threshold is met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose controlled transactions between the French SAS and foreign related parties, including purchases, sales, services, royalties, financing, guarantees, and restructurings. Amounts must reconcile to the statutory accounts and local transfer-pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate income tax balance after crediting instalments and allowable credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment must be made electronically from the French taxpayer's tax account or through an authorized payment arrangement. A foreign parent should not pay or net the amount without preserving an auditable intercompany settlement record.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filed corporate tax returns generally attract a 10% surcharge, increased to 40% for deliberate failure and 80% for fraudulent maneuvers or abuse of rights. Late-payment interest is generally 0.20% per month, subject to statutory rules. Failure to use mandatory electronic filing or payment channels may trigger separate fixed penalties. Inaccurate returns may also generate reassessment, interest, penalties, and loss of tax benefits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2067-SD, relevé des frais généraux, where applicable; Form 2258-SD, country-by-country report, where the French reporting entity and group satisfy the applicable threshold and reporting conditions; electronic filing through EDI-TDFC or the designated French tax administration channel.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The applicable information return generally follows the corporate tax return deadline. The country-by-country report is generally due within 12 months after the end of the reporting fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Specified categories of high-value remuneration, travel, entertainment, and other general expenses where the statutory reporting conditions are met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report French SAS expenditure even where the beneficiary or service provider is non-resident. Maintain invoices, business purpose evidence, approval records, and withholding tax analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Country-by-country revenue, profit, taxes, employees, tangible assets, and group entities by tax jurisdiction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The French SAS should not independently prepare a group report unless it is the designated reporting entity or a secondary filing obligation applies. Obtain the group filing reference and preserve evidence of the reporting entity and notification status.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to provide required transfer-pricing or country-by-country information may lead to a penalty of up to 0.5% of the transactions concerned or 5% of the reassessed profits, subject to statutory conditions and minimum amounts. General tax penalties, reassessment interest, and criminal exposure may also apply for materially false or incomplete information.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: The standard French withholding tax on dividends distributed by a French company to a non-resident is generally 25%, subject to applicable exemptions, tax treaties, and anti-abuse rules. A 0% domestic exemption may apply to qualifying distributions to an EU or EEA parent company holding at least 10% of the French payer for the required period, or providing an appropriate commitment, if the statutory conditions and anti-abuse requirements are met. A 75% rate may apply to payments to certain non-cooperative jurisdictions or territories.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's foreign tax authority, verify beneficial ownership, legal form, minimum holding, holding period, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose requirements, and anti-abuse conditions, and retain the corporate ownership chain and supporting documents. Apply the reduced treaty or EU Parent-Subsidiary rate only when the payer has sufficient evidence. Otherwise withhold at the domestic rate and allow the recipient to seek a refund using the relevant French refund forms and treaty documentation. Declare and pay withholding through the applicable French withholding return and payment process by the statutory deadline.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French-source royalties paid to non-residents are generally subject to a domestic withholding tax of 25%, subject to treaty reduction or exemption and specific rules for non-cooperative jurisdictions. Interest paid by a French company is generally not subject to ordinary French withholding tax, but exceptions apply, including payments to certain non-cooperative jurisdictions and certain regulated or instrument-specific cases. Treaty rates vary and commonly reduce royalty withholding to approximately 0% to 10% and interest withholding to approximately 0% to 10%. Treaty access requires residence, beneficial ownership, eligible income characterization, and anti-abuse support.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 150 million. A French entity meeting the applicable turnover or gross-asset threshold, or belonging to a group meeting the relevant statutory conditions, may be required to maintain comprehensive transfer-pricing documentation, including a Master File and Local File, and to provide it to the tax administration. A country-by-country reporting obligation generally applies to multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million. A transfer-pricing policy summary may be required under the applicable Form 2257-SD rules.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate a single, separately branded economic substance regulation equivalent to certain offshore ESR regimes. Substance is enforced through the arm's-length principle, abuse-of-law doctrine, principal-purpose and beneficial-ownership tests, controlled foreign company rules, anti-hybrid rules, interest limitation, permanent-establishment principles, withholding tax anti-abuse provisions, and general anti-avoidance rules. A French SAS manufacturing instant rice noodles should maintain genuine French personnel, production capacity, premises, inventory, quality-control functions, decision-making, risks, assets, banking records, and commercial rationale. Conduit entities, circular financing, unsupported management fees, and contractual arrangements inconsistent with actual functions may be challenged.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting French sales, fabricating expenses, concealing inventory or production, issuing false invoices, or using sham transactions to reduce corporate income tax or value added tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, late-payment interest, a penalty of up to 80% of the avoided tax, and criminal tax-fraud sanctions generally including up to five years' imprisonment and a EUR 500,000 fine. Aggravated cases may carry up to seven years' imprisonment and a EUR 3 million fine, subject to statutory conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may face criminal prosecution, personal tax liability in cases of fraudulent or repeated obstruction under French tax procedure law, civil restitution, management disqualification, and confiscation. Travel restrictions may be imposed only under applicable judicial or enforcement measures; they are not an automatic tax penalty.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Fraudulent insolvency and abuse of corporate form
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Asset stripping, preferential payments, concealment of assets, diversion of company funds, continuation of knowingly loss-making operations, or transferring the French SAS's business to a related entity to defeat creditors or the tax administration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil liability for all or part of the company's insufficient assets, clawback of transactions, bankruptcy-related sanctions, management bans, and potential criminal penalties for specified insolvency offenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be ordered to contribute to the shortfall, prohibited from managing companies, and prosecuted personally. The limited-liability shield does not protect fraudulent conduct, personal guarantees, commingling, or deliberate mismanagement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length royalties, management fees, financing costs, procurement margins, or product prices; shifting French manufacturing profit to a foreign affiliate without corresponding functions, assets, and risks; or failing to document controlled transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment under the arm's-length principle, denial of deductions, withholding tax exposure, interest limitation adjustments, penalties for inadequate documentation, and potential 40% or 80% tax penalties where intent or fraud is established.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur personal exposure where they knowingly approve false records, fraudulent declarations, asset diversion, or conduct causing tax loss. Ordinary transfer-pricing adjustments do not automatically create personal criminal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing dividends, interest, or royalties through an intermediary with no substantive activity, misrepresenting tax residence, using a nominee recipient, or claiming treaty relief without beneficial ownership or commercial purpose.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty or EU exemption, recovery of withholding tax, interest, penalties up to 80% in aggravated cases, and potential anti-abuse or abuse-of-law proceedings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly certify false treaty eligibility may face tax-fraud, document-fraud, or aiding-and-abetting exposure, in addition to civil restitution and management sanctions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Value added tax and customs fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Under-reporting domestic sales, falsely claiming export or intra-EU exemptions, manipulating customs values or origin, using fictitious importers, or deducting input VAT on non-business or fabricated invoices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of VAT, customs duties, excise and import charges, interest, penalties generally ranging from 10% to 80% depending on conduct, customs penalties, seizure, and criminal prosecution for serious fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal criminal liability, customs-related sanctions, civil recovery, management bans, and confiscation where they participated in or knowingly facilitated the scheme.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained cash or third-party payments, disguising beneficial owners, processing circular trade payments, ignoring suspicious counterparties, or failing to maintain customer, supplier, and payment due diligence appropriate to the business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal money-laundering liability may include up to five years' imprisonment and a EUR 375,000 fine, with aggravated or organized cases carrying materially higher penalties. Assets may be frozen or confiscated, and regulatory or professional sanctions may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may be prosecuted for participation, concealment, facilitation, or failure to prevent unlawful transactions where legally applicable. Confiscation, civil restitution, management disqualification, and judicial travel restrictions may follow.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining parallel books, falsifying inventory counts, backdating invoices, recording fictitious expenses, concealing related-party transactions, or approving accounts that materially misstate the French SAS's financial position.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Accounting and corporate-law sanctions, tax reassessment, criminal penalties for specified false-accounting conduct, auditor reporting obligations, and potential insolvency or tax-fraud proceedings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The president, directors, de facto managers, and participating officers may incur criminal, civil, and management-ban liability. A corporate form does not shield intentional falsification or personal participation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlawful profit extraction and dividend distribution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends without distributable profits, disguising distributions as loans or management fees, paying dividends while the company is insolvent, or failing to withhold and remit tax on cross-border distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Repayment of unlawful distributions, corporate tax and withholding tax recovery, interest, penalties, director liability, and possible criminal sanctions for misuse of corporate assets or fraudulent distribution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The president and approving officers may be personally liable for restitution, creditor losses, tax amounts, and misuse-of-corporate-assets offenses. Judicial management bans and confiscation may apply in serious cases.
